stem: What does this five-sided sign warn you about?
choices: A pedestrian mall where cars are not allowed
A playground for adults
A school zone or school crossing
A hospital zone
oneLineConcept: Five-sided sign: school zone or school crossing
explanation:
The **five-sided (pentagon) sign** warns of a **school zone or school crossing**. Watch closely for **children**, and remember that in many school zones the **speed limit is lower** during school hours.

**Wrong choices**
- A playground for adults: The five-sided shape is used for schools, not adult play areas.
- A hospital zone: Hospitals are shown on blue service signs.
- A pedestrian mall where cars are not allowed: This sign warns of children crossing; it does not close the road to cars.

stem: What does this yellow warning sign mean?
choices: You are entering a one-way street
Traffic ahead moves in both directions on the same road
Two lanes going your way are ahead
Passing is allowed in both lanes ahead
oneLineConcept: Two-way traffic sign: oncoming traffic shares the road
explanation:
The two arrows point in **opposite directions**, so the sign warns that **traffic moves both ways** ahead. You will share the road with **oncoming vehicles**, so stay on your side.

**Wrong choices**
- You are entering a one-way street: A one-way street is marked with a black and white ONE WAY sign.
- Two lanes going your way are ahead: Two lanes going the same way would show arrows pointing the same way.
- Passing is allowed in both lanes ahead: The sign shows opposite traffic; it does not say passing is allowed.
imageAlt: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a black border. It shows two thick black vertical arrows side by side. The left arrow points down and the right arrow points up.

imageSource.title: MUTCD (FHWA) sign W6-3
imageSource.license: U.S. federal government work, public domain

stem: What does this yellow warning sign mean?
choices: A car wash is ahead
The road has sharp curves for several miles
The road is slippery when wet
Loose gravel may hit your windshield
oneLineConcept: Car with wavy tracks: slippery when wet
explanation:
The sign shows a **car with wavy skid marks** behind it. It warns that the road is **slippery when wet**. In rain, **slow down**, increase your following distance, and avoid sudden braking or steering.

**Wrong choices**
- A car wash is ahead: Businesses such as car washes are not marked with warning signs.
- The road has sharp curves for several miles: Curves are shown with a curved arrow, not a car with skid marks.
- Loose gravel may hit your windshield: This sign is about traction on a wet road, not flying gravel.
imageAlt: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a black border. It shows the back of a black car with two wavy black lines trailing below it, one under each rear wheel.

imageSource.title: MUTCD (FHWA) sign W8-5

stem: What shape are most warning signs?
choices: Octagon
Upright rectangle
Diamond
Circle
explanation:
Most warning signs are **diamonds**, normally **black on yellow**. They warn of a **hazard or change** in the road ahead.

**Wrong choices**
- Octagon: The octagon is used only for STOP.
- Circle: The round sign is used for the railroad advance warning.
- Upright rectangle: Upright rectangles are mostly used for rule signs, such as speed limits.

stem: What does an orange diamond-shaped sign with black letters tell you?
choices: A construction or maintenance work zone is ahead
A rest area is ahead
The speed limit is about to rise
A school zone is ahead
explanation:
**Orange signs with black messages** are used only for **work zones**. When you see one, **stay alert**, slow down, and be ready for lane shifts, workers, and flaggers.

**Wrong choices**
- A school zone is ahead: School signs are yellow-green with five sides.
- A rest area is ahead: Rest areas are shown on guide signs.
- The speed limit is about to rise: Speed limits are shown on white rule signs.

stem: What does a round yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR mean?
choices: Right lane closed
A rest room is nearby
Road repairs are ahead
A railroad crossing is ahead
oneLineConcept: Round yellow RR sign: railroad crossing ahead
explanation:
The **round yellow sign** with an **X and RR** gives **advance warning of a railroad crossing**. **Slow down**, look and listen, and be ready to stop.

**Wrong choices**
- Road repairs are ahead: Road work is shown with orange work zone signs.
- Right lane closed: A lane closure is shown on a diamond or rectangular sign with words or lane symbols.
- A rest room is nearby: Rest rooms are shown on blue service or guide signs.

stem: Where is the X-shaped crossbuck sign placed?
choices: About a mile before the railroad crossing
At the railroad crossing itself
On the train
Only at crossings with gates
oneLineConcept: Crossbuck: at the railroad crossing itself
explanation:
The **crossbuck** is a white X-shaped sign reading RAILROAD CROSSING. It stands **at the crossing itself**. A smaller sign below it shows if there is **more than one track**.

**Wrong choices**
- About a mile before the railroad crossing: The round yellow RR sign is the advance warning before the crossing.
- Only at crossings with gates: Crossbucks are used at crossings with or without gates.
- On the train: The sign stands beside the road, not on the train.

stem: What does a yellow STOP AHEAD warning sign tell you?
choices: A STOP sign is ahead that may be hard to see
The road ends
You must stop at this sign
A police checkpoint is ahead
oneLineConcept: STOP AHEAD: a hidden STOP sign is coming
explanation:
**STOP AHEAD** is a warning sign placed well before a STOP sign when a **curve or other objects block your view** of it. Begin **slowing down** so you can stop at the STOP sign.

**Wrong choices**
- You must stop at this sign: The warning sign itself is not where you stop; you stop at the STOP sign.
- A police checkpoint is ahead: The sign warns of a STOP sign, not a checkpoint.
- The road ends: A road that ends has its own warning sign.

stem: On which side of the road is the yellow no-passing pennant posted?
choices: On either side, depending on the county
The right side
The left side
Above the center of the road
oneLineConcept: No-passing pennant: left side of the road
explanation:
The yellow **pennant** is posted on the **left side of the road**, where a driver about to pass will see it. It **points to where the no-passing zone begins**, where a solid yellow line starts in your lane.

**Wrong choices**
- The right side: The DO NOT PASS rule sign is on the right; the pennant is on the left.
- Above the center of the road: The pennant is mounted at the roadside, not over the road.
- On either side, depending on the county: Its placement does not change by county.

stem: What shape is the warning sign that marks the start of a no-passing zone?
choices: A pennant (a long triangle on its side)
A pentagon
A circle
A diamond
explanation:
The **no-passing zone** sign is a yellow **pennant**, a long triangle lying on its side. It **adds emphasis** to the rectangular DO NOT PASS rule sign.

**Wrong choices**
- A diamond: Diamonds are used for most other warning signs.
- A circle: The circle is used for the railroad advance warning.
- A pentagon: The pentagon is used for school signs.

stem: In a work zone, a flagger holds up a paddle that says STOP. What should you do?
choices: Slow down and go around the flagger
Stop and wait until the flagger signals you to go
Honk and continue slowly
Stop only if you see workers on the road
oneLineConcept: Flagger's STOP paddle: stop and wait
explanation:
Work zone flaggers use a **STOP/SLOW paddle** to control traffic. When the paddle shows **STOP**, you must **stop and wait** until the flagger lets you go.

**Wrong choices**
- Slow down and go around the flagger: Driving around a flagger who shows STOP is dangerous and illegal.
- Stop only if you see workers on the road: The flagger's signal applies whether or not you can see workers.
- Honk and continue slowly: Honking does not give you permission to go.

stem: Where does a highway work zone begin and end?
choices: It begins at the first cone and ends at the last worker
From the first sign marking the start of the work zone to the last sign marking its end
Within 500 feet of any construction equipment
Only where workers are present that day
oneLineConcept: Work zone: from the first sign to the last sign
explanation:
A highway work zone is the area **between the first sign** that shows the **start** of the work zone and the **last sign** that shows its **end**. The posted work zone speed limit applies in that whole area.

**Wrong choices**
- It begins at the first cone and ends at the last worker: Cones and workers do not set the legal limits; the signs do.
- Only where workers are present that day: The work zone exists even when no workers are visible.
- Within 500 feet of any construction equipment: There is no fixed 500-foot rule; the signs mark the zone.

stem: You see a yellow diamond with black symbols and then an orange diamond with black symbols. What is the difference?
choices: Both are warnings, but orange ones warn of construction or maintenance work
Yellow signs are rules; orange signs are suggestions
Orange signs are for trucks only
Yellow signs apply only at night
oneLineConcept: Yellow diamond: general warning; orange: work zone warning
explanation:
Both are **warning signs** with the diamond shape. **Black on yellow** warns of general hazards, while **black on orange** warns of **construction or maintenance areas**, so drive with extra care.

**Wrong choices**
- Yellow signs are rules; orange signs are suggestions: Neither color is a rule sign; both are warnings you should heed.
- Orange signs are for trucks only: Orange work zone signs apply to all drivers.
- Yellow signs apply only at night: Yellow warning signs apply at all hours.

stem: Which of these is NOT shown on a five-sided (pentagon) sign?
choices: School zone
Railroad crossing ahead
School crossing
Children near a school
oneLineConcept: Railroad advance warning is round, not five-sided
explanation:
The **five-sided sign** warns of a **school zone or school crossing**, where children may be present. A **railroad crossing ahead** is shown by a **round** yellow sign with an X and RR, not a pentagon.

**Wrong choices**
- School zone: This is shown on a five-sided sign.
- School crossing: This is shown on a five-sided sign.
- Children near a school: The five-sided sign warns that schoolchildren may be present.

stem: You are about to pass on a two-lane road and see a yellow pennant on the left side. What should you do?
choices: Pass only if the car ahead is going under the speed limit
Finish passing quickly before the solid line starts
Move into the left lane and wait there
Do not start to pass, because a no-passing zone begins
oneLineConcept: Pennant: do not start a pass into a no-passing zone
explanation:
The pennant **points to the start of a no-passing zone**, where a **solid yellow line** begins on your side. **Do not begin a pass** that you cannot finish before that point.

**Wrong choices**
- Finish passing quickly before the solid line starts: Rushing to pass at the start of a no-passing zone is dangerous and illegal.
- Pass only if the car ahead is going under the speed limit: A slower car ahead does not make it legal to pass in a no-passing zone.
- Move into the left lane and wait there: Driving in the oncoming lane while waiting is very dangerous.

stem: What does the small sign under a railroad crossbuck show?
choices: That there is more than one track
The name of the railroad
The speed of the next train
The time of the next train
oneLineConcept: Sign under the crossbuck: number of tracks
explanation:
A smaller sign **below the crossbuck** shows when there is **more than one track** at the crossing. After one train passes, **another may be coming** on a different track.

**Wrong choices**
- The speed of the next train: Train speed is not posted at crossings.
- The name of the railroad: The railroad's name and an emergency number appear on the blue emergency sign, not under the crossbuck.
- The time of the next train: Train schedules are not posted on crossing signs.

stem: You are on a two-lane road and see a diamond sign with two arrows pointing in opposite directions. What should you expect?
choices: The next lane is for passing only
The road becomes one-way
Oncoming traffic will share the road with you
You must turn around
oneLineConcept: Two-way traffic sign: expect oncoming vehicles
explanation:
Two arrows pointing in **opposite directions** on a yellow diamond warn of **two-way traffic** ahead. Expect **oncoming vehicles** and **stay to the right** of the center line.

**Wrong choices**
- The next lane is for passing only: The sign does not set aside a passing lane.
- The road becomes one-way: The sign warns of the opposite: traffic will move both ways.
- You must turn around: The sign is a warning, not an order to turn around.
